stĭpŭlātus , ūs, m. id., jurid. t. t.,
I.a
promise formally demanded; a bargain, stipulation, Quint. Decl. 12, 21: “si quid adversus pactionem fiat, non ex stipulatu agitur, etc.,” Gai. Inst. 3, 94 ; 4, 116; Dig. 45, 1, 1; 45, 1, 4 sq.; 45, 1, 103 sq.; Paul. Sent. 5, 7, 2 sq. al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
